title: Central TermAl host crashed: "memory allocation of 2719744 bytes failed" (0xc0000409) at 17:08Z during the Engram baa6 Windows FULL
outcome: The Central host does not die when system commit runs low: test-run placement keeps enough commit headroom for the host through a commit-based floor, and the host's abort on a failed allocation is carried by w-ee06482f6d8e. The cause of the 17:08Z commit exhaustion is identified from the retained measurements, with the unmeasured per-process split recorded as such.
acceptance: The 2026-11-14 17:08:27Z crash is explained from the retained evidence, with proven facts and inferences marked: commit charge reached the system commit limit (os error 1455 and LNK1102 in the crash minute), the charge already present at launch (the limit minus the launch free-commit census), and the increment from the Engram baa6 Windows FULL's 24-job link phase. A per-process split of the charge at crash time (rustc/test, Node, Chrome, the host itself) is recorded as not measured and not reconstructable from the retained evidence.
Central placement rules (capacity memory central-cargo-memory-budget) cover FULLs on Central with a commit-based floor that would have prevented this, recorded and applied by the integration owner.
If the host's own abort on allocation failure is avoidable (for example a bounded allocation on a hot path), that is filed or fixed separately with a behavioural test.
